title: Simultaneous equations: two clues, one answer
examples: How do you solve simultaneous equations?
Why do you need two equations for two unknowns?

left.label: Taco
left.ask: Why do you need two equations?

explain.say: At a school fair you pay in tokens. Lucia pays 10 tokens for 2 tacos and 1 juice. Look at the balance. One clue, but two mystery prices. Can you find them from this clue alone? Not yet!

draw.text: Simultaneous equations: two clues, one answer

left.label: Taco
left.ask: Why do you need two equations?

explain.say: Then Ben pays 7 tokens for 1 taco and 1 juice. Here is the second clue on its balance. Can you spot what is different between the two orders?

left.label: Juice
left.ask: How do you find the second unknown?

explain.say: Lucia bought just one extra taco, and paid 3 more tokens. So one taco costs 3 tokens! Taking one clue away from the other like this is called elimination.
Now put the taco price into Ben's order. 3 plus the juice makes 7. So the juice costs 4 tokens. Look at the juice box on the balance.

left.label: Juice
left.ask: How do you find the second unknown?

explain.say: Fantastic detective work! Check Lucia: 3 plus 3 plus 4 is 10. Yes! Wow: the GPS in a phone solves equations like these with signals from several satellites to find where you are. Challenge: 3 pens and 1 ruler cost 11, 1 pen and 1 ruler cost 5. Find each price.

left.label: Taco
left.ask: Why do you need two equations?

faq.q: Why do you need two equations?
faq.a: One equation with two unknowns has many possible answers. A second clue narrows it down to just one pair that fits both.
asks: Why can't you solve it with one equation?

faq.a: You add or subtract the equations to remove one unknown. Lucia's order minus Ben's order removes the juice and leaves 1 taco equals 3 tokens.

faq.q: How do you find the second unknown?
faq.a: Put the value you found back into either equation. 3 plus juice equals 7, so the juice is 4. This is called substitution.
asks: What do you do after finding one unknown?

faq.q: How do you check simultaneous equations?
faq.a: Put both values into both equations. 2 times 3 plus 4 is 10, and 3 plus 4 is 7, so both clues work.
asks: How do I check my answer?

faq.q: Why do the lines cross at the answer?
faq.a: Each equation makes a straight line on a graph. The point where they cross is the only pair of values that fits both equations.
asks: What do simultaneous equations look like on a graph?

facts: Two straight lines that cross meet at exactly one point, which is the solution of their simultaneous equations.
Parallel lines never meet, so their simultaneous equations have no solution.

quiz.say: 3 pens and 1 ruler cost 11. 1 pen and 1 ruler cost 5. How much is one pen?
quiz.why: Take the second clue from the first: 2 pens cost 6, so one pen costs 3.

wrong.2: 6 is the cost of 2 pens, not one.

quiz.say: x plus y equals 10 and x minus y equals 2. What is x?
quiz.why: Add the equations: 2x equals 12, so x is 6, and y is 4.

wrong.2: 8 is 10 minus 2, which mixes up the steps.
